comparison: Both evaluate the C. elegans connection (C8, C42-C51, C59) with perfect claim overlap. OpenEval finds the theoretical modeling and experimental data convergent and SUPPORTED despite unidentified sensors. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the connection but criticizing lack of systematic rigor and noting the work 'does not succeed in formalising nor addressing any particular open questions.'

Both evaluate experimental practice claims (C20-C21) with perfect agreement. OpenEval and peer review both rate SUPPORTED, recognizing these as well-established methodological observations about genome editing and RNAi that justify simulation design choices.

Both evaluate information density claims (C52-C54) with perfect claim overlap. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to C52's lack of empirical support for maximal genome information density. Peer review rates SUPPORTED, not directly challenging these mechanistic claims, though they relate to the broader DNA comparison critique.

Both evaluate differential response and heritability claims (C4-C5, C19, C22-C24, C58) with high overlap. OpenEval finds simulation evidence directly SUPPORTED. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, acknowledging 'convincing examples' but criticizing lack of systematic study and statistical rigor in outcome classification.

Both evaluate enumeration and mutational connectivity (C25-C30) with high overlap. OpenEval finds data and inferences SUPPORTED. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, praising the attention to architecture mutations as 'excellent' but questioning the DNA comparison as 'somewhat tenuous' and fairness of the genetic-epigenetic comparison.

OpenEval R1 addresses combinatorial information scaling (C2, C14-C18, C57, C60-C61) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R2 evaluates overlapping enumeration claims (C14-C18, C27, C57, C60-C61) but rates UNCERTAIN, challenging the DNA comparison as 'unfair' regarding basic unit definitions while not disputing enumeration itself.

OpenEval R2 addresses minimal HRA structure and theoretical justification (C3, C11-C13, C56, C62-C64) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R1 evaluates overlapping foundational claims (C1-C3, C11-C13, C55-C56, C62-C64) also rated SUPPORTED, with reviewers acknowledging this as accepted theoretical basis and praising 'attention paid to how one architecture mutates into another.'

Both evaluate C. elegans developmental timing integration (C37, C40-C41) with moderate overlap. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED despite stringent constraints (11/10,000 stable systems). Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, citing inadequate description of the stochastic model and insufficient methodological detail for reproduction.

Both evaluate negative regulation requirements (C31-C34) with moderate overlap. OpenEval finds core simulation results SUPPORTED with logical speculative extensions. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, criticizing sudden model changes from Figure 4 onwards, unexplained stochasticity, and insufficient SI detail for reproduction.

OpenEval R5 includes periodic rescue and somatic-germline claims (C6-C7, C35-C36) that overlap with peer R6. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with speculative extensions. Peer R6 rates SUPPORTED, with editor acknowledging the 'novel aspect' of unifying non-genetic inheritance across unicellular and multicellular contexts.

OpenEval R8 addresses transgenerational context (C1, C9-C10, C55) with partial overlap to peer R10's biological context claims (C9-C10, C38-C39). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on citations and enumeration. Peer R10 rates SUPPORTED, accepting background claims that motivate the theoretical framework.

OpenEval R8 includes foundational claims (C1, C55) that minimally overlap with peer R1's theoretical framework evaluation. Both rate SUPPORTED, with peer review acknowledging the manuscript 'explores conditions for epigenetic inheritance' as foundational basis.

OpenEval R7 includes biological context (C37-C39) with minimal overlap to peer R10. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for integration of realistic timing. Peer R10 rates SUPPORTED for background citations, not challenging these contextual claims.

OpenEval R3 includes diagnostic value claim (C58) that minimally overlaps with peer R12. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for complementary diagnostic value. Peer R12 rates UNCERTAIN, noting lack of systematic study challenges the claimed diagnostic utility.

OpenEval R4 includes information capacity interpretation (C27) that minimally overlaps with peer R2's enumeration evaluation. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED. Peer R2 rates UNCERTAIN, questioning the DNA comparison framework that contextualizes this capacity claim.

OpenEval R1 includes theoretical framework claim (C2) that minimally overlaps with peer R1's foundational evaluation. Both rate SUPPORTED, with peer review accepting the theoretical basis for the work.
